title: DataAccessV1dot10
description: K-05 v1.10, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1240, from the D-017 path audit's rulings R3 and R4, QUESTIONS.md CQ-200 and CQ-61; DL-492). It only adds to v1.9 (data-access.v1.9.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to v1.8, v1.7, v1.6, v1.5, v1.4, v1.3, v1.2, v1.1 and v1): every v1.9 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none changes, so every v1 to v1.9 exchange is a v1.10 exchange. Added: three reads on the runtime side the first staging turn's receipt and its clock arming need, which no call named (README items 49 to 51): readQuestionFacts, the facts the clock arming's due rule reads about one open question (its Clock line, its business's zone, the visit it is about, its never-delivered row: runtime/src/clocks/types.ts QuestionFacts; open gap 25; CQ-200); readHandle, a K-04 handle's kind and address by its id, from which the consumer names the handle's actor with the gateway's own rule (actorNameOf: CQ-200); and readChatHandle, the phone handle a Linq chat id names, the number a delivery receipt belongs to, or none (adapters/src/linq/webhook/parse.ts ParseLookups.chatHandle; CQ-61). Each runs as rosie_job with no business scope, reads the primary uncached, writes nothing and reads K-04 v1's rows as migrated (0001 to 0031) with the grants rosie_job holds, so no column, grant, index or migration is added. Not here: the handle's party for a turn (partyOf), which a decision this version does not hold leaves to a later minor version (open gap 55). Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

questionVisit.title: QuestionVisit
questionVisit.description: The visit an open question is about, as the clock arming's due rule reads it (README item 49; runtime/src/clocks/types.ts QuestionFacts.visit): its booking's flow and its start. The booking is the question's own (K-04 v1 open_questions.booking_id), read at the question's business, and its start is the earliest lower bound of K-04 v1 reservations.during among that booking's reservations that are held or booked (README default 90). It carries no visit address and no address zone: K-30 v1 holds them, and its tables are not migrated (0001 to 0031 hold none), so v1.10 reads neither, and no K-05 answer carries an address (README default 91; rule 7). New in v1.10.

flow.description: K-04 v1 bookings.flow as stored: A, the customer comes to the business; B, the business goes to the customer (RULES 2.1). The due rule's zone reads it (CQ-05, CQ-08; S13-03).

startsAt.description: The visit's start, UTC: the earliest lower bound of during among the booking's held or booked reservations (K-04 v1 reservations by booking_id, reservations_booking_idx; README default 90). No clock runs past it (S13-35; arch 02 line 127: 'unless that passes the visit's start, which always comes first').

neverDeliveredRow.title: NeverDeliveredRow
neverDeliveredRow.description: The question's never-delivered clock row (K-04 v1 clock_rows of kind never_delivered whose open_question_id is the question's) with the version read, which the arming cancels once the question is delivered, compared and set on that version (K-05 v1 item 5, cancelClock; runtime/src/clocks/arming.ts). Of several, the one waiting or armed with the lowest id, else the one with the lowest id, ids compared, never parsed (README default 92; CQ-09). New in v1.10.

version.description: The row's version as read, which the arming's cancelClock compares (expectVersion).

readQuestionFacts.request.title: ReadQuestionFactsRequest
readQuestionFacts.request.description: The facts the clock arming's due rule reads about one open question, beyond its receipt (README item 49; runtime/src/clocks/types.ts QuestionFacts and QuestionFactsReader; T-255's due rule, runtime/src/clocks/due.ts; open gap 25; QUESTIONS.md CQ-200): its Clock line, its business's zone, the visit it is about and its never-delivered row. The arming (C-055) sends it when the dispatcher hands it a first delivery (markPart's firstDelivery, or v1.9's repeatedDelivery.firstOfRow), naming the question by the openQuestionId markPart's answer gives, never by anything in the receipt. The request names the question alone: its business, its booking and its zone are read from the question's own row, so no caller names another business's (refuse-question-facts-caller-business). Scope: the runtime side, as rosie_job with no business scope, as armClock and cancelClock run (README 'Scope'), each read of a business-scoped table naming the question's own business. Reads the primary, uncached (arch 02 line 117: decision reads). Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: inside the gateway's 1 s for the receipt (arch 02 line 109), beside markPart and armClock. New in v1.10.

openQuestionId.description: K-04 open_questions.id: the question markPart's answer names (openQuestionId), whose clock row the arming arms.

readQuestionFacts.response.title: ReadQuestionFactsResponse
readQuestionFacts.response.description: The question's facts, each as K-04 v1 stores it (README item 49): the Clock line as it applies, its business's zone, the visit it is about and its never-delivered row, in the port's own names (runtime/src/clocks/types.ts QuestionFacts), so the binding maps them across and gives the port's visit addressZone and address null (README default 91). Never an address, a number or anything of another business. New in v1.10.

openQuestionId.description: The question read, as the request names it.

clockLine.description: K-04 v1 open_questions.clock as stored: the step's Clock line as it applies, such as '24 h' (K-05 v1 openQuestionNew.clock); null when the step has none, so step 9's default applies (arch 02 line 127; T-255's due rule).

businessZone.description: K-04 v1 businesses.time_zone of the question's business (open_questions.business_id); null for a question with no business, a sign-up's before S1-09 writes one (CQ-05: the visit's zone, else the business's; with neither the due rule takes UTC).

visit.description: The visit the question is about (questionVisit); null for a question about no booking (open_questions.booking_id null) and for a booking with no held or booked reservation, which has no time (README default 90).

neverDelivered.description: The question's never-delivered clock row with its version (neverDeliveredRow); null when it has none, as every question has until a commit makes one (STATE note 37: turn 1's commit makes none).

readQuestionFacts.errors.title: ReadQuestionFactsErrors
readQuestionFacts.errors.description: notFound (table open_questions): no question has the id, so the arming arms nothing and reports it (runtime/src/clocks/arming.ts: questionNotFound); transient: the same request may be sent again. A read writes nothing. New in v1.10.

readQuestionFacts.exchange.title: ReadQuestionFactsExchange
readQuestionFacts.exchange.description: One readQuestionFacts request with its outcome: the question's facts, or one of its errors. New in v1.10.

readHandle.request.title: ReadHandleRequest
readHandle.request.description: A K-04 handle by its id, for the name of its actor (README item 50; QUESTIONS.md CQ-200; runtime/src/wiring/real.ts ArmingCalls.actorNameOf; runtime/src/clocks/actors.ts actorOf). The clock arming after armClock arms a row its handle owns, and the minute sweep and staging's Fire now for a row they hand to its actor (T-254, T-255), send the clock row's handle id, as K-05 answers it (armClock's clock.handleId; K-04 clock_rows.handle_id). The consumer names the handle's actor from the answer with the gateway's own rule (runtime/src/gateway/seal.ts actorNameOf, '<kind>:<address>'), never with another (README default 93). Scope: the runtime side, as rosie_job with no business scope (K-04 handles is scoped none, and rosie_job is the role that reads it: 0012). Reads the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: inside the gateway's 1 s for a receipt's arming (arch 02 line 109); none in the sources for the sweep. New in v1.10.

handleId.description: K-04 handles.id, never an address (K-08 v1 handleRef).

readHandle.response.title: ReadHandleResponse
readHandle.response.description: The handle the id names, as K-04 v1 handles stores it (kind and address, in K-06 v1's handle shape, the one the gateway names an actor by), or null when K-04 holds no handle with that id, which the consumer reads as no actor (actorNameOf answers null: README default 95). The address is a phone number or an email address: the consumer uses it only to name the actor, and never logs it or puts it in a span or an entry (rule 7). New in v1.10.

handleId.description: The handle asked for, as the request names it.

handle.description: K-04 handles.kind and handles.address (K-06 v1 handle; handles_address_form: an E.164 number or a lower-case email address); null when no handle has the id.

readHandle.errors.title: ReadHandleErrors
readHandle.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again. A handle K-04 does not hold is an answer (handle null), not an error (README default 95). New in v1.10.

readHandle.exchange.title: ReadHandleExchange
readHandle.exchange.description: One readHandle request with its outcome: the handle, or none, or transient. New in v1.10.

chatPhoneHandle.title: ChatPhoneHandle
chatPhoneHandle.description: The handle a Linq chat belongs to: a phone, as K-04 v1 handles stores it (K-06 v1 handle with kind phone and the number in E.164 form). A Linq event comes from a phone (K-06 v1: 'A Linq event comes from a phone', arch 01 line 55), and the adapter takes only an E.164 number for a receipt (adapters/src/linq/webhook/parse.ts receiptHandle), so the answer never names an email handle (refuse-chat-handle-email; README default 94). New in v1.10.

kind.description: A Linq chat's handle is a phone (K-04 handles.kind).

address.description: The number in E.164 form (K-04 handles_address_form), which the receipt's K-06 event carries as its handle (K-06 v1 handle: 'that Rosie's part went to for a receipt').

readChatHandle.request.title: ReadChatHandleRequest
readChatHandle.request.description: The phone handle a Linq chat id names (README item 51; QUESTIONS.md CQ-61; adapters/src/linq/webhook/parse.ts ParseLookups.chatHandle; runtime/src/wiring/real.ts LinqVerifyInputs). A delivery receipt, Rosie's own reaction and a failed poll carry Linq's chat id, not the person's number, while their K-06 event names 'the handle Rosie's part went to', so the gateway's Linq verify (C-044) asks this read for the chat's handle before the event is built, and answers 503 for a receipt it cannot place, so Linq retries (CQ-61's default). The request names the chat id alone. Scope: the runtime side, as rosie_job with no business scope (K-04 threads and handles are scoped none: 0012). Reads the primary, uncached. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: inside the gateway's 1 s (arch 02 line 109). New in v1.10.

linqChatId.description: Linq's chat id as the webhook carries it (K-06 v1 chatId; K-04 threads.linq_chat_id, threads_linq_chat_key: one thread at most). Never logged, put in a span or an entry (K-09 v1.5 default 135).

readChatHandle.found.title: ReadChatHandleFound
readChatHandle.found.description: The chat's thread (K-04 threads of kind chat whose linq_chat_id is the request's) belongs to a phone handle: its id and its number (README item 51). New in v1.10.

handleId.description: K-04 threads.handle_id, the handle the chat is with (K-08 v1 handleRef).

readChatHandle.unknown.title: ReadChatHandleUnknown
readChatHandle.unknown.description: No chat thread of a phone handle holds the chat id: no thread holds it (a number whose chat thread no commit wrote: open gap 48), or the thread or its handle is of another kind (README default 94). Both fields null: the adapter answers receiptHandleUnknown and the gateway 503, so Linq retries (CQ-61), and a receipt is never placed on a guessed handle. New in v1.10.

readChatHandle.response.title: ReadChatHandleResponse
readChatHandle.response.description: The chat's phone handle, or none (README item 51). An unknown chat is an answer, not an error (README default 95). New in v1.10.

readChatHandle.errors.title: ReadChatHandleErrors
readChatHandle.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again; the gateway answers 503 meanwhile and Linq retries (arch 02 line 109). New in v1.10.

readChatHandle.exchange.title: ReadChatHandleExchange
readChatHandle.exchange.description: One readChatHandle request with its outcome: the chat's phone handle, or none, or transient. New in v1.10.
